overall_summary: Analysis of 44 deduplicated Shorts reveals a clear bifurcation: first-person hypothetical space survival scenarios ('What If You Fell Into...') and extreme exoplanet environments generate 700-1,000+ views and 20-38 likes, whereas recycled brain/psychology facts and verbatim re-uploads ('Fake Memories', 'Songs Stuck in Head', duplicated 'Octopus Hearts') languish below 100 views with near-zero engagement. Viewer retention and virality heavily favor visceral cosmic hazards.

winning_patterns.pattern: First-Person Extreme Cosmic Immersion ('What If You Fell Into...')
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes) lead all videos in reach and engagement.
winning_patterns.action: Adopt high-stakes first-person hypothetical framing placing the viewer into lethal cosmic anomalies with precise sensory physics.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,030 views, 36 likes) and 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (981 views, 21 likes) dramatically outperform general biological or psychological trivia.
winning_patterns.action: Target bizarre planetary dynamics and extreme physical thresholds rather than mundane nature facts.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' uploaded multiple times peaked at 53 views down to 5 views; 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' got only 38 views and 0 likes.
weak_patterns.action: Discontinue generic psychology micro-tips; they fail to stop scrolling feeds.

weak_patterns.evidence: Repeatedly posting identical scripts ('Why Space Is Completely Silent', 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts') dilutes impressions and yields inconsistent bottom-tier views.
weak_patterns.action: Enforce strict novelty; never re-upload verbatim concept variations.

next_video.hook_style: High-Stakes First-Person Hypothetical ('What If You Stood...')
